name: Dark Cadet Blue
lede: Dark Cadet Blue is a muted, darker modifier on [[cadet-blue|cadet blue]] — itself named for the grayish blue of a military cadet's uniform — scanned from Ridgway's 1912 plates and filed by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955.

sections.title: A darker cadet blue
sections.body:
The name follows the library's modifier grammar, *dark* plus [[cadet-blue|cadet blue]], whose own name comes from the grayish blue of a military cadet's uniform [1]. Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* records this hue twice, at plate XXI, hue 49′ and again at plate XXXIV, hue 47″, both scans of aged plates and so only approximate; the ISCC-NBS system filed the chip in 1955 as a moderate blue [1].

Its nearest named neighbors are [[newport]], almost the same at 3.0 units, and [[denim]], a touch more vivid at 3.2 [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color this close to Dark Cadet Blue is common in our archive: 210 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, about 0.88 percent, more common than 58 percent of the named colors [3]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, at 2.9 times the expected rate, and most often plays an accent, 34 percent of the time [3]. The earliest match dates to 1350, by the Master of San Lucchese, 562 years before the name's own 1912 record [3]. That is centuries before the name's own record, a floor on the hue's age, not a first use of either the name or a pigment.
